title: Intent-based routing mapper and probabilistic fallback sequencer
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Scope: Refactor the routing policy engine to introduce an intent->route mapper and a probabilistic fallback sequencer that together simplify authoring and improve graceful degradation under capacity pressure.

Goals:
- Surface an explicit 'intent' layer in the DSL to decouple business intent from implementation routing rules (region, tier, model-variant).
- Provide a compact, validated schema for intent declarations that map to a prioritized set of candidate route patterns.
- Implement a lightweight probabilistic sequencer that selects fallback model variants or regions based on capacity signals, weighted SLO objectives, and customer tier.
- Keep backwards compatibility with the current routing DSL via a compatibility adapter and staged migrations.

Out of scope: full policy transpiler rewrite, autoscaling changes, and long-term analytics integration (these are tracked in follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: New DSL additions for 'intent' compile cleanly and pass schema validation for all existing examples
Compatibility adapter retains identical decisions for 99.9% of historical routes in the synthetic decision replay (log-replay test)
Probabilistic sequencer exposes tunable weights and respects customer-tier hard constraints (no downgrade for enterprise tier without override)
Unit + integration tests for mapper + sequencer achieve >= 90% coverage and run in CI under 90s
Performance regression: end-to-end route decision latency increase <= 1.5ms at p95 under synthetic load (measured on pipeline-labs instance)
Canary rollout plan documented and automated via feature flag with automatic rollback on error budget burn > 10%
notes: 2026-02-18 - Created: Initial spike showed intent layer reduces rule count by ~28% on sample corpora (Asha).
2026-02-23 - Spike findings: Two styles of intent definitions emerged (declarative weights vs. explicit ordered lists). Decided to support both but prefer weights for new rules to enable sequencer.
2026-03-01 - Design review: PM (Jorge) requested a way to tag intents with business-critical metadata (billing_tier + regulatory_flag). Added to schema draft.

2026-03-03 - Engineering discussion: Trade-off between fully deterministic fallback ordering and probabilistic sequencing. We chose probabilistic sequencing with a deterministic override per-customer to balance fairness and SLO targets.
2026-03-04 - Security review kickoff: passed initial threat model; required KMS checks for intent metadata encryption in Private deployments.
2026-03-06 - Implementation: Added a 'compatibility adapter' module that rewrites legacy route rules into the interim intent form. Adapter lives behind feature flag 'intent_adapter_v1'.

2026-03-08 - Perf test: Baseline route decision microbenchmark shows +0.9ms p95 delta when sequencer enabled with default weights; within acceptable threshold. Test harness: pipeline-labs/routing-bench.

2026-03-09 - Code review notes (from reviewer Mei Chen): request to extract capacity signal sampler to an interface for easier unit testing; also flagging a potential thread-safety issue in KV cache access path during adapter replay. Assigned follow-ups.
2026-03-10 - Next steps: Address code review points, add end-to-end canary script (console integration), and schedule a 10% customer canary for runtime-1.22 in week 2026-W13.
